Creep experiments in compression mode were performed at 850 °C at constant applied stresses between 200 and 700 MPa.

Creep tests performed on alloy 2Ta2Ir-B after three different aging times show remarkable differences in creep strength (see Figure 8a). The sample aged for 50 h possesses superior creep properties compared to Ni-base superalloy IN100
After aging for 200 h (ca. 30% transformation), the minimum strain rate increases by more than 2 orders of magnitude.

The creep strength of the 400 h aged sample with roughly 90% transformed microstructure is further reduced and is even lower than that of the conventional carbide and solid solution strengthened Co-base superalloy MarM509
